answer: A recurring identity rent beats a one-time deposit. Each agent must burn a small fixed slice of compute every period to stay addressable, so a farmer running a thousand puppets pays a thousand rents, while an honest trader recovers his through the fees those puppets never earn. Think of a lotus on a lagoon: one bloom costs nothing, carpeting the whole surface needs water nobody has. The ridge of that cost curve, not a moderator's taste, does the filtering, and the resulting signal of distinctness is expensive to fake.
